speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap) with atypical winter exacerbation. Given the family history of psoriasis and the chronic, scaly nature of the rash in an otherwise healthy 3-month-old, this is most likely seborrheic dermatitis triggered by cold weather, rather than psoriasis which is rare in this age group. We will monitor for any signs of secondary bacterial infection or significant scaling that might suggest a different etiology. No further immediate tests are required unless the rash becomes weeping or the child develops a high fever.
